title: 1、INT. RAVENSWOOD THEATER - STAGE - DAY.
content:
FADE IN:

INT. RAVENSWOOD THEATER - STAGE - DAY

A grand old proscenium theater in mid-renovation. Scaffolding in the wings, paint buckets pushed aside. House lights fully up.

DIANA CRANE (40s, razor-focused, dark blazer) stands center stage gripping a RED CLIPBOARD, scanning a cue sheet. Her pen taps a fast rhythm against the board.

Enter LEON MARSH (30s, tall, effortlessly magnetic) from stage left. His LEFT ARM is in a white plaster CAST from wrist to elbow. He carries his script in his right hand.

LEON
Diana. Can we revisit the Act Two blocking? The cast makes the movement feel wrong.

DIANA
Prop issue. Talk to Priya.

PRIYA NAIR (20s, efficient, quick-moving) appears from the wings. She wears a YELLOW LANYARD looped around her neck -- keys, radio fob, and access cards dangling from it. She carries a tablet.

PRIYA
I heard my name. What is the disaster?

LEON
Not a disaster. An adjustment.

OSCAR VANE (60s, silver-haired, deliberate) enters from the back of the house carrying a worn LEATHER BRIEFCASE. He climbs the stage stairs and sets it on a prop table.

OSCAR
Are we working or discussing working?

DIANA
Both, apparently. Oscar, I need you on the Scene Nine revision.

Oscar opens his leather briefcase. Inside: the thick script, marked in three colors of ink.

DIANA (CONT'D)
(to the room)
Full run-through at four. Everyone ready.

title: 2、INT. RAVENSWOOD THEATER - GREEN ROOM - DAY.
content:
INT. RAVENSWOOD THEATER - GREEN ROOM - DAY

A comfortable room off the stage wing. Mirrors, makeup stations, a battered couch. The cast is scattered about. Diana stands at the front, red clipboard to her chest.

DIANA
Opening night is FRIDAY. That is five days. Not six. Not seven. Five.

Murmurs from the cast.

DIANA (CONT'D)
We have four hundred seats to fill. Each of those is a person who paid for something extraordinary.

She looks at Leon.

DIANA (CONT'D)
Leon. The arm. Story?

LEON
(sighing)
I was fixing a light in my apartment. The ladder slipped. I fell off the ladder. That is the whole story.

DIANA
You fell off a ladder.

LEON
I fell off a ladder.

OSCAR
(dryly)
The leading man.

LEON
The leading man who will be fully healed by closing night, thank you.

Priya raises her hand.

PRIYA
For the record, I told him twice to call building maintenance.

LEON
For the record, I prefer to handle things myself.

Leon glances around the room.

LEON (CONT'D)
First production I have done here, for the record. Good to finally work at Ravenswood.

DIANA
And we are glad to have you. Now -- Act Three. Places in ten minutes.

title: 3、INT. RAVENSWOOD THEATER - OFFICE - DAY.
content:
INT. RAVENSWOOD THEATER - PRODUCTION OFFICE - DAY

A cluttered room. Script pages pinned to every surface. A whiteboard covered in timelines. On the counter, a COFFEE MACHINE bears a handwritten OUT OF ORDER sign.

Diana sits across from Oscar, who spreads the script on the desk. The title page reads: A QUIET MACHINE -- written by OSCAR VANE.

OSCAR
Three acts. The structure is deliberate. Remove the intermission and the psychological rhythm collapses.

DIANA
I understand the rhythm, Oscar. I am asking about running time.

OSCAR
Three acts. One intermission. One hundred and forty minutes. That is the script as written by me and that is how it stays.

Diana's phone RINGS. She pulls it from her pocket -- an old NOKIA FLIP PHONE, its case cracked down one side. She flips it open.

DIANA
(into phone)
Yes. Friday. No -- we have talked about this.

She claps it shut and tosses it on the desk.

OSCAR
(eyeing the phone)
Do they still manufacture those?

DIANA
It works. That is enough.

She reaches toward the COFFEE MACHINE before catching sight of the OUT OF ORDER sign.

DIANA (CONT'D)
Forgot. Again.

OSCAR
There is a place two blocks down.

DIANA
No time.

She returns to the desk and picks up the script.

title: 4、INT. RAVENSWOOD THEATER - STAGE - EVENING.
content:
INT. RAVENSWOOD THEATER - STAGE - EVENING

The house lights dimmed to half. Priya moves efficiently between prop tables, inventorying items on her tablet.

She lifts a SILVER-PAINTED PROP PISTOL from the table, checks it against her list, and places it in the prop cabinet. She closes the cabinet and secures it with a PADLOCK, spinning the dial three full rotations before engaging the lock.

Leon approaches, watching.

LEON
Doing the full inventory tonight?

PRIYA
Padlocked. Done. This close to opening night, nothing walks off.

LEON
Wise policy.

A pause. Priya gives him a look.

PRIYA
You want to run the pistol scene.

LEON
Just the draw. The cast makes the motion feel strange.

PRIYA
(sighing)
Five minutes.

She opens the padlock, retrieves the silver prop pistol, and hands it to Leon. He stands in position, right hand raising the pistol smoothly.

LEON
The line is: "Put it down before one of us stops breathing." Then the draw.

He moves through it. Power there, even with the left arm in the cast.

PRIYA
That actually works.

LEON
I told Diana.

Priya takes the pistol, returns it to the cabinet, and locks the padlock again with three spins.

PRIYA
Don't tell anyone I let you practice without a spotter.

title: 5、EXT. RAVENSWOOD THEATER - ALLEY - NIGHT.
content:
EXT. RAVENSWOOD THEATER - ALLEY - NIGHT

Diana steps out through a side door into the narrow alley behind the theater. A man is already there. BRAM HOLLOWAY (50s, precise, well-dressed) checks his watch as she approaches.

BRAM
Ms. Crane. I have been waiting.

DIANA
We are mid-rehearsal.

BRAM
Which is why I waited outside.

Diana crosses her arms.

DIANA
You said there was a funding matter.

BRAM
Fifty thousand dollars. Cash transfer, cleared before opening night. In return: a seat in the box on Friday and a mention in the program.

Diana stares.

DIANA
Fifty thousand.

BRAM
Fifty thousand dollars.

A long silence. A cab passes the mouth of the alley.

DIANA
Why? You have never shown interest in theater.

BRAM
I am interested now.

DIANA
And your terms are only what you said. Box seat. Program credit.

BRAM
That is all.

Diana considers. Then:

DIANA
I will have the paperwork by morning.

BRAM
I look forward to Friday.

He steps away into the dark. Diana watches him go, then looks back at the lit windows of the theater.

DIANA
(to herself)
Fifty thousand dollars.

title: 6、INT. RAVENSWOOD THEATER - GREEN ROOM - DAY.
content:
INT. RAVENSWOOD THEATER - GREEN ROOM - DAY

Next morning. The green room is quieter. Leon sits at a makeup station reviewing his script. Oscar reads in the corner.

DIANA enters, consulting a BLUE CLIPBOARD. She sets it on the table and turns to Leon.

DIANA
Leon. The stage physician cleared you for full movement. Any pain, you stop.

LEON
Understood. Honestly, the whole thing was a fluke. I was in a car accident -- the other driver ran a red light. Lucky it was just the arm.

DIANA
Right.

She makes a note on the blue clipboard.

OSCAR
(not looking up)
Car accident. I thought it was the ladder.

LEON
Does the cause matter?

OSCAR
Not to the production. Only to the story you tell.

Leon says nothing. Diana glances between them and marks something else on the blue clipboard.

DIANA
Full company on stage in thirty minutes. I want Act One clean.

title: 7、INT. RAVENSWOOD THEATER - OFFICE - DAY.
content:
INT. RAVENSWOOD THEATER - PRODUCTION OFFICE - DAY

Diana is at the desk. OSCAR enters carrying a CANVAS BACKPACK, which he drops over the back of a chair.

DIANA
I moved opening night. It is Saturday now. The new funding required one additional rehearsal day.

OSCAR
Saturday.

DIANA
Saturday. Eight o'clock curtain.

Oscar sits and pulls the script from his canvas backpack. Diana's SMARTPHONE buzzes on the desk. She picks it up and scrolls.

DIANA (CONT'D)
(into phone)
Yes, confirmed Saturday. Eight o'clock.

She sets the phone down and crosses to the COFFEE MACHINE. She pours herself a cup and drinks.

OSCAR
Leon came to me this morning. He was cheerful.

DIANA
Good.

OSCAR
I signed his cast. He seemed to want it.

DIANA
How is that relevant to opening night?

OSCAR
He was protecting the right side all morning. More than the left.

DIANA
He is compensating.

OSCAR
I signed the right arm. He held it out specifically.

Diana pours a second cup of coffee and does not respond.

title: 8、INT. RAVENSWOOD THEATER - STAGE - NIGHT.
content:
INT. RAVENSWOOD THEATER - STAGE - NIGHT (DRESS REHEARSAL)

The house is dark except for stage lights. A handful of production staff sit in the front rows taking notes.

PRIYA approaches the prop cabinet and unlocks it with a SMALL KEY from her lanyard. She removes a GOLD-PAINTED PROP PISTOL and brings it to Leon in the wings.

LEON
(checking the weight)
Feels the same.

PRIYA
Properties said the silver was too reflective under stage lights. Gold reads better at distance.

Leon pockets the gold-painted pistol.

In the house, Oscar settles into a front-row seat beside Diana.

OSCAR
(low)
Six hundred seats and every one of them empty tonight.

DIANA
They will not be empty Saturday.

OSCAR
Let us hope so.

The rehearsal proceeds through a long sequence. At the end of a tense dramatic section:

DIANA
(calling to the stage)
End of Act Four! Take five, everyone!

The cast relaxes on stage. Leon sets the gold-painted pistol on the nearest prop table.

title: 9、EXT. RAVENSWOOD THEATER - ENTRANCE - NIGHT.
content:
EXT. RAVENSWOOD THEATER - ENTRANCE - NIGHT (OPENING NIGHT)

The marquee is lit. A crowd mills outside. Programs are handed out at the door.

Diana stands at the entrance greeting guests. BRAM approaches in a dark coat.

DIANA
Mr. Holloway. Thank you. Your seventy-five thousand dollars made all of this possible.

BRAM
(nodding)
Glad to be part of it, Ms. Crane.

He accepts a program and moves inside. Diana turns to greet others.

Nearby, PRIYA coordinates ushers. She wears a BLUE LANYARD tonight, laminated access cards hanging from it in place of the usual keys.

On the wall near the entrance doors, a framed PRODUCTION POSTER shows the cast list. At the bottom in smaller print: STARRING LEON MARSH IN HIS FIFTH PRODUCTION AT RAVENSWOOD THEATER.

A GUEST picks up a PROGRAM from the welcome table and opens it. The credits page reads clearly: A QUIET MACHINE -- Written by WILLIAM HARNESS.

Inside, the house fills. The lobby lights begin to dim.

PRIYA
(into her radio)
Full house. Ready on your mark.

FADE OUT.

END OF STORY.
